implement.approach: Regression suite first (commit 876c941b, base run 8 failed / 2 passed of 10), one follow-up test commit (cf36afc3: findNodeHandle resolution through the RN Jest View class mock, since react-test-renderer node mocks never reach a ref under the preset), then the implementation commit (c6861581). ceremonyRequest.ts gains a process-wide surface registry: claimSurface(kind)/release, presentedSurfaceId(), subscribeToSurfaces() and the useSurfaceSlot(kind, wanted, generation) hook. Preempting kinds (permission sheet, paywall route) win immediately because they are already on screen; product-owned kinds (notice, ceremony) wait for the slot, a presented one keeps it, and on release the highest priority waiter (notice before ceremony, then FIFO) is presented. CeremonyHost claims the 'ceremony' slot while it has or wants a presentation, releases/re-claims after every dismissal (generation = completed count) so a queued error notice goes before the next queued ceremony, treats losing the slot as ineligibility (presentation cleared WITHOUT complete(), so the request survives and is re-presented as a new presentation id when the slot returns), records the trigger captured by openCeremonyFrom() on the request and calls AccessibilityInfo.setAccessibilityFocus(findNodeHandle(trigger)) once the presentation is gone, and exposes announce() through the presentation context; useCeremonyAnnouncement(message) dedupes by (presentation id, message) so relayout/re-measure re-renders stay quiet while a new step or a new presentation announces again. Owner-generation and stale-request fencing are unchanged (ceremonyArbitration 27/27).

implement.summary:
W09-04 round 2 on branch devin/pp/w09-04/impl-r2 (HEAD e0c19d1113c17e1d30934778faff94c93fc501ab, pushed to origin; no PR opened, nothing pushed to main or ci/mac-*, mac-full-verify not run). Started from BASE 55d80326, cherry-picked the three sound r1 commits (eee0e3c5 suite, ea0829ad mock, 9a9d56e0 arbiter/focus/announce), then added two commits: da8852de (regression tests) and e0c19d11 (fix).

Defects on the r1 candidate (BASE has no arbiter, so the objective was not met there at all): (1) P0 — apps/mobile/src/flow/CeremonyHost.tsx (r1 line 262) called react-native findNodeHandle(trigger) in the dismissal effect on the HostInstance captured by openCeremonyFrom(); when the Settings 'Replay walkthrough' row had unmounted before Skip (sign-out content swap, or ready=false remount), RN throws 'Unable to find node on an unmounted component.' and RootErrorBoundary crashes the tree. The r1 suite's RendererProxy mock stubbed findNodeHandle so it never saw this. (2) P1 — apps/mobile/src/flow/ceremonyRequest.ts (r1 lines 52, 76-79) put 'paywall' in a PREEMPTING set that outranked 'notice', and BrandNoticeHost renders visible only when presented, so the paywall's own 'Terms of use / Privacy policy could not be opened' notice (RootNavigator openLegalPage → showBrandNotice) was withheld until the paywall closed and then popped out of context; r1's own test pinned that behaviour.

Fix (write_paths only): ceremonyRequest.ts now models permission/paywall as BlockerKind with an explicit WITHDRAWS table — permission withdraws ['notice','ceremony'], paywall withdraws ['ceremony'] only — and ranks slot kinds by PRIORITY (notice 0, ceremony 1) with FIFO tiebreak; a presented slot that is still eligible keeps the screen. useSurfaceSlot is typed to SlotKind. New exported restoreFocusToTrigger(trigger): boolean wraps findNodeHandle in try/catch, returns false for null handles or thrown 'unmounted' errors, and only then calls AccessibilityInfo.setAccessibilityFocus; CeremonyHost's dismissal effect calls it instead of findNodeHandle directly, so a stale trigger is ignored and the dismissal/store completion proceed. Tests: RendererProxy mock now runs the real findNodeHandle first so unmounted triggers throw as on device; added stale-trigger (ownerKey unchanged, and sign-out swap → sign-in remount) tests asserting no throw and no setAccessibilityFocus call; added Paywall→Terms-of-use-fails test asserting the danger notice is visible while paywall content stays mounted; rewrote the r1 test that pinned the withheld notice to assert the notice shows at once while the competing ceremony still waits.

review.summary: APPROVE W09-04 candidate devin/pp/w09-04/impl-r2 @ e0c19d1113c17e1d30934778faff94c93fc501ab (reviewed_sha = git rev-parse HEAD). The other 8 (RankUpCelebration, StreakCelebration, BrandNotice, design/components, notificationStore, PaywallScreen, SettingsScreen, FirstRunWalkthrough) are each listed in out_of_scope_files, are under no serial_group_paths prefix, and are the minimum producer-side wiring without which the arbiter would be an uncalled module: ceremonies claim the 'ceremony' slot via CeremonyHost, BrandNoticeHost claims 'notice' and renders `visible={notice !== null && presented}`, notificationStore wraps the only production requestPermission call sites in claimSurface('permission') with release in finally, PaywallScreen claims 'paywall' for its mount lifetime, SettingsScreen passes the Replay row ref through openCeremonyFrom, PressableScale forwards a HostInstance ref (React 19 ref-as-prop), and the three announcers route through useCeremonyAnnouncement for per-presentation dedupe. scope_violation=false. Shipping composition VERIFIED by reading: RankUp/Streak/Walkthrough hosts and BrandNoticeHost render under the root tree, so the arbiter is exercised by shipping code. DIFF REVIEW vs REVIEW.md/AGENTS.md: no comment lines removed or edited in src (grep of removed lines); no @ts-ignore/any/eslint-disable/.skip/.only/passWithNoTests/|| true/setTimeout inflation/forceExit in added lines; no user-facing copy added (announcement strings are existing walkthrough/rank/streak copy; no Android/Google Play/guest/Live Court/DUPR/superlative/accuracy claims); no touch of billing, access/permits, RLS, migrations, session/auth, owner generation or diagnostics transport — the change is purely UI arbitration, so billing conservation and owner-isolation invariants are unaffected. Owner isolation in CeremonyHost is preserved (eligible() still requires current.ownerKey === ownerKey and isDataOwnerContextCurrent; sign-out/sign-in remount test pins it). Arbitration model: BlockerKind permission withdraws ['notice','ceremony'], paywall withdraws ['ceremony'] only (so the paywall's own Terms/Privacy failure notice shows immediately over it); slot PRIORITY notice 0 < ceremony 1 with FIFO tiebreak and a still-eligible presented slot keeps the screen; claims are released in effect cleanup / finally so no leaked blocker was found. Focus: dismissal stores the trigger, and a post-null-presentation effect calls restoreFocusToTrigger which try/catches findNodeHandle and only calls setAccessibilityFocus for a non-null handle. Announcements: dedupe keyed by (presentation id, message), re-announced on a new presentation (tested). Non-blocking notes: best-effort focus with no fallback landing element when the trigger unmounted; walkthrough re-presents from step 1 after a permission preemption (outside write_paths, disclosed); on-device VoiceOver behaviour is UNKNOWN from Linux (no Mac run performed, per hard rules). Zero blocking issues; zero invariant violations. No PR opened, nothing pushed, no Mac runner used. Review logs kept at artifacts/review-w09-04/ (gitignored) and uploaded as attachments.
